subject: mitosis

composition.story: Mitosis replicates a cell into two identical daughter cells through coordinated steps. Chromosomes condense, align at the center, separate to opposite poles, and finally the cell divides completely.

aha.observation: Sister chromatids split apart and migrate toward opposing spindle poles, doubling the genetic material count at each side.

states.label: Prophase
states.sentence: Chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

states.label: Metaphase
states.sentence: Chromosomes align along the metaphase plate, attached to spindle fibers.
states.why: Ensures equal segregation in the next phase.

states.label: Anaphase
states.sentence: Sister chromatids are pulled apart toward opposite poles by shortening spindle fibers.

states.label: Telophase
states.sentence: Two new nuclear envelopes form around the separated sets and chromosomes decondense.
states.why: Restores resting state for two independent cells.
